questions.q: Why, according to the editorial, does force fail to end a movement built on an idea?
options: Leaders are too well protected
Not quite. The article says: An idea outlives its leaders; it can be answered only by a better idea.
Ideas spread only in secret
Not quite. The article says: An idea outlives its leaders; it can be answered only by a better idea.
Force is never used firmly enough
Not quite. The article says: An idea outlives its leaders; it can be answered only by a better idea.
An idea outlives its leaders; it can be answered only by a better idea
Yes. Hence the call for a counter-ideology.
questions.rationale: “It is not possible to bring an end to the influence of an ideology by force. Even if some leaders are hanged, new leaders will emerge and keep the ideology alive.”

questions.article: From Planet Earth to Planet Paradise
questions.q: Stephen Hawking suggested mankind should settle on other planets. What does the article offer as the Quran’s view of man’s future home?
options: Mankind will remain on earth for ever
Not quite. The article says: The earth is a temporary abode; the lasting home to prepare for is Paradise.
The earth is a temporary abode; the lasting home to prepare for is Paradise
Right. One must become a deserving candidate for it.
The future cannot be known at all
Not quite. The article says: The earth is a temporary abode; the lasting home to prepare for is Paradise.
Another planet has been made ready for us
Not quite. The article says: The earth is a temporary abode; the lasting home to prepare for is Paradise.
questions.rationale: “The earth has been made as a temporary abode for human beings… Then the other abode for humans would be Paradise.”

questions.q: What solution does the article propose for quarrels over “who is the boss,” for example at home?
options: Avoid any shared work
Not quite. The article says: Be your own master in thought, and for practical matters be willing to let the other person lead.
Decide by turns who gives the orders
Not quite. The article says: Be your own master in thought, and for practical matters be willing to let the other person lead.
Let the elder always decide
Not quite. The article says: Be your own master in thought, and for practical matters be willing to let the other person lead.
Be your own master in thought, and for practical matters be willing to let the other person lead
Yes. Cooperation is a must in practical life.
questions.rationale: “In theoretical matters, take yourself as your own boss; but in practical matters, as per your convenience, accept the other person as the boss.”

questions.q: The article contrasts treating religion as something to be “followed” with treating it as something to be “imposed.” Why does the difference matter?
options: Following is private; imposing is more sincere
Not quite. The article says: Following turns a person to reforming himself; imposing turns him against rulers and so towards violence.
Following turns a person to reforming himself; imposing turns him against rulers and so towards violence
Well reasoned. The aim is the individual, not the state.
There is no real difference in practice
Not quite. The article says: Following turns a person to reforming himself; imposing turns him against rulers and so towards violence.
Following is for the weak; imposing for the strong
Not quite. The article says: Following turns a person to reforming himself; imposing turns him against rulers and so towards violence.
questions.rationale: “If Islam is the subject to be followed, then the goal is to focus on oneself… But when Islam is considered a subject of imposition, the goal then becomes the external political system… Here lies the root of violence.”

questions.article: A Training Course in Thanksgiving and Piety
questions.q: Fasting is described as training with a dual purpose. What are the two?
options: Health of the body, and saving of money
Not quite. The article says: Gratitude for God’s blessings, and taqwa – holding back from what He forbids.
Gratitude for God’s blessings, and taqwa – holding back from what He forbids
Correct. “The whole life of the believer is a life of fasting.”
Memorising scripture, and learning its language
Not quite. The article says: Gratitude for God’s blessings, and taqwa – holding back from what He forbids.
Charity to neighbours, and hospitality to guests
Not quite. The article says: Gratitude for God’s blessings, and taqwa – holding back from what He forbids.
questions.rationale: “Fasting is training with a dual purpose. One is thanksgiving, the other Taqwa (righteousness or piety).”

questions.q: What common mistake about God does the article describe?
options: Believing that He hears prayer
Not quite. The article says: Imagining Him on the pattern of human beings – for example, as needing intermediaries or favouring one group.
Thinking of Him as the Creator of all
Not quite. The article says: Imagining Him on the pattern of human beings – for example, as needing intermediaries or favouring one group.
Holding that He is One
Not quite. The article says: Imagining Him on the pattern of human beings – for example, as needing intermediaries or favouring one group.
Imagining Him on the pattern of human beings – for example, as needing intermediaries or favouring one group
Yes. Such beliefs are called a negation of His divinity.
questions.rationale: “He visualises God in his image and vice versa. Human history is the story of this mistake and its consequences.”

questions.q: A young man’s news of his promotion at work reminded the author of something greater. What?
options: The reward of a long life
Not quite. The article says: Entry into heaven – promotion from this imperfect world to the perfect one.
The author’s own early career
Not quite. The article says: Entry into heaven – promotion from this imperfect world to the perfect one.
Entry into heaven – promotion from this imperfect world to the perfect one
Right. So one should weigh one’s actions before they are weighed.
The honour paid to scholars
Not quite. The article says: Entry into heaven – promotion from this imperfect world to the perfect one.
questions.rationale: “Entry into heaven also is a promotion. People whose record in this imperfect world is found to be good will be promoted and allowed to enter into the perfect world of heaven.”

questions.q: How does the article describe the relation between Ramazan and the other eleven months?
options: Ramazan is for preparation through study of the Quran; the rest of the year is for sharing its message
Yes. That is why its reward is unlimited.
Ramazan is for travel; the other months for home
Not quite. The article says: Ramazan is for preparation through study of the Quran; the rest of the year is for sharing its message.
Ramazan is for charity; the other months for saving
Not quite. The article says: Ramazan is for preparation through study of the Quran; the rest of the year is for sharing its message.
Ramazan is for rest; the other months for work
Not quite. The article says: Ramazan is for preparation through study of the Quran; the rest of the year is for sharing its message.
questions.rationale: “The month of Ramazan—is meant for preparation and the remaining eleven months are for spreading the message of the Quran to all mankind.”

questions.q: Why, according to the article, is it harder to be clear about ideas than about physical things?
options: Ideas are less important than things
Not quite. The article says: Physical things come already separate in nature; ideas lie mixed in the mind and must be sorted by analysis.
Words for ideas do not exist
Not quite. The article says: Physical things come already separate in nature; ideas lie mixed in the mind and must be sorted by analysis.
Physical things never change
Not quite. The article says: Physical things come already separate in nature; ideas lie mixed in the mind and must be sorted by analysis.
Physical things come already separate in nature; ideas lie mixed in the mind and must be sorted by analysis
Well read. Objective, unprejudiced thinking is needed.
questions.rationale: “In contrast to material objects… ideas do not exist separately. They exist in our minds mixed up along with other ideas.”

questions.q: On what basis, according to the article, did Islam teach human equality?
options: All people should own the same amount
Not quite. The article says: The only distinction is between God and man; every human being is equally His servant.
All people have the same abilities
Not quite. The article says: The only distinction is between God and man; every human being is equally His servant.
All people belong to one nation
Not quite. The article says: The only distinction is between God and man; every human being is equally His servant.
The only distinction is between God and man; every human being is equally His servant
Exactly. Distinctions among people fall away.
questions.rationale: “It stressed that the distinction was between God and man, and that there was no distinctions between human beings. Every human being, it taught, was a servant of God.”
